STELLAR EVOLUTION: FREE STREAMING VERSUS TRAPPING Helioscope and stellar bounds on axions assume that axions produced in a star leave it freely. For the couplings required here this is not necessarily the case. In this section we consider cases where axions do not leave the star efficiently. The conclusion is that trapping does not help: the Sun excludes the model for any perturbative gae. All the estimates are approximate, using the solar centre of the standard solar model [69]: Tc ≃ 1.35 keV, ρc ≃ 150 g cm−3 for the central temperature and density, and a Rosseland opacity Kγ ∼ 1 cm2 g−1 , so that the photon mean free path is λγ = 1/(Kγρ) ∼ 10−2 cm, with ρ the local density. We write Ka and λa = 1/(Kaρ) for the corresponding axion quantities. Axion opacity. Due to their coupling to electrons, gae, axions are absorbed by the same electron processes that generate the photon opacity.
